required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A disaster/resilience scenario cannot pass if disaster response access, recovery access, insurance access, mitigation access, tribal/rural access, disability access, or emergency service availability falls below reviewed floors.

A disaster/resilience scenario cannot pass if lower costs are achieved by degrading life safety, warning quality, response timeliness, recovery quality, mitigation quality, or claims/service integrity.

A disaster/resilience scenario cannot pass if disaster risk, unmet need, delays, insurance gaps, recovery burden, or mitigation exclusion shifts to lower-income, rural, tribal, disabled, elderly, or historically underserved communities without review.

A disaster/resilience scenario cannot pass if reserve adequacy, response capacity, recovery continuity, mitigation coverage, infrastructure resilience, or emergency override capacity falls below reviewed floors.

A disaster/resilience scenario cannot pass without event-normalized outlays, exposure and damage denominators, base/supplemental bridge, declaration-to-account-to-outlay bridge, reserve rule, implementation cost, and delivery feasibility.

disaster_resilience_specific_floor_defin.definition: Life safety, warning, evacuation, emergency response, and immediate shelter floors require sourced baseline, policy, and stress values before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Recovery timeliness, continuity of public services, housing stability, and claims/service access require explicit reviewed floors.
Mitigation coverage, infrastructure hardening, avoided-loss methodology, and resilience capacity require sourced floor values before policy scoring.
Unmet need, recovery delay, insurance gap, mitigation access, and burden distribution require reviewed floors by income, geography, tribal status, disability, age, and other vulnerability dimensions.
Prefunded reserve contributions, withdrawals, caps, emergency overrides, and stress capacity require explicit parameters before solver use.

No target cost can be selected without exposure-normalized loss distribution, event-normalized outlays, base/supplemental bridge, declaration-to-account-to-outlay bridge, reserve rule, implementation cost, and delivery feasibility.

public_warning_phrases: This disaster/resilience floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.
Declarations are not spending, project amounts are not outlays, benefit-cost ratios are not realized savings, and none is a fraud finding.

No lower-cost disaster/resilience scenario is admissible until life safety, recovery continuity, mitigation/resilience, equity/unmet need, reserve adequacy, exposure-normalized loss distribution, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No target cost, reserve path, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not an exposure-normalized loss distribution, not an event-normalized outlay path, not a prefunded reserve rule, not a declaration-to-outlay bridge, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
